problem: LLMs struggle to automate optimization by bridging the gap between real-world requirements and mathematical formulations or effective heuristic designs, especially for NP-hard problems.
approach: OptMaster structures optimization as a DAG where each node represents a candidate solution, enabling cross-branch knowledge transfer; it replaces textual self-reflection with verification code to suppress hallucinations and ground evaluation in deterministic computation.
contribution: OptMaster achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on formulation benchmarks and surpasses best known solutions on Circle Packing (n=26, 32) and achieves a cut of 9,590 on Gset70.

problem: Current Omni-MLLMs lack systematic and comprehensive evaluation of their audio-visual intelligence capabilities despite recent advances in integrating vision, audio, and language.
approach: AVI-Bench evaluates Omni-MLLMs across three cognitive stages (perception, understanding, reasoning) through cross-modal audio-visual tasks; AVI-Bench-PriSe extends this with unfamiliar low-semantic stimuli to test generalization.
contribution: Extensive experiments reveal substantial limitations in current Omni-MLLMs and present a four-level AVI taxonomy to guide development of more robust and generalizable audio-visual intelligence.

problem: Mendelian Randomization relies on untestable instrumental variable assumptions that are often violated in practice when genetic variants correlate with environmental factors, leading to confounding between instruments and outcomes.
approach: A representation learning framework exploits multi-environment genetic data to recover latent exogenous components of genetic instruments suitable for causal inference.
contribution: The approach provides theoretical insights into when learned components act as valid instruments and demonstrates effectiveness through simulations and semi-synthetic experiments using the All of Us Biobank.

problem: Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models rely on 2D images, limiting spatial understanding in complex scenes and robustness across different environments and depth scales.
approach: Any3D-VLA unifies simulator, sensor, and model-estimated point clouds into a training pipeline to construct diverse 3D inputs and learns domain-agnostic 3D representations fused with 2D representations.
contribution: Simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate Any3D-VLA improves performance and mitigates domain gap in robotic manipulation tasks.
